subject: Career
title: Tailoring for Every Application
description: A short lesson to help you apply Tailoring for Every Application.

hook.text: Sending the same resume to every job is like wearing a tuxedo to every occasion.

buildup.text: Each job posting emphasizes different priorities. Your resume should mirror those priorities.

discovery.text: Read the posting's top three requirements. Reorder your bullets so those shine first.

twist.text: You're not lying — you're curating. The same career can tell different true stories.

climax.text: A base resume plus 15 minutes of tailoring outperforms a generic one every time.

punchline.text: One resume for all jobs impresses none.

quiz.question: What does tailoring a resume mean?
options: Reordering bullets to match the job's priorities

details.summary: Tailoring your resume for each application means adjusting keywords, emphasized skills, and bullet point order to match the specific job description. A generic resume sent to every opening performs significantly worse than targeted versions.
details.whyItMatters: Recruiters and ATS systems evaluate fit to a specific role. A generic resume may contain all the right content but fail because the relevant information is not prioritized for that particular position.
takeaways: Customize your summary and top bullet points for each application
Mirror the job description's exact terminology in your resume
Maintain a master resume and create tailored versions for each target

faq.question: How much should you change your resume for each job application?
faq.answer: At minimum, adjust your summary statement and reorder bullet points to lead with the most relevant accomplishments. For significantly different roles, you may need to swap out bullets entirely. Keep a master resume of all accomplishments and select the most relevant subset for each application.

faq.question: Is it worth the time to tailor your resume when applying to dozens of jobs?
faq.answer: Yes. Ten tailored applications produce better results than fifty generic ones. If you must prioritize, at least customize for your top-choice roles. The tailoring time is invested in quality over quantity, which yields higher interview conversion rates.
